assumptions: Tỷ VND. Bệnh viện giả lập Lộc Tâm. Toy donor-funded equipment recognized gross as PPE; conditional capital grant deferred and released over equipment life. Không hoàn grant nếu vận hành đúng; không thuế.

evidence.text: [Biên bản nhận tài trợ] Donor trả 80 tỷ cho thiết bị trị giá 120 tỷ. Bệnh viện bỏ cash 40. Điều kiện grant: duy trì thiết bị cho community care 5 năm; toy ghi deferred grant, release theo depreciation. Grant đã nhận đủ.
[Sổ PPE] Equipment ready July1, life 5 years straight-line, zero residual. Không impairment. Chi phí đào tạo staff 3 tỷ trả tháng 6, expensed; không nằm PPE.
[Hoạt động] 6 tháng cuối năm cung cấp 4.000 procedures có phí 8 triệu/case và 1.000 charity procedures không phí. Cost variable 4 triệu/case cho mọi procedure.
[Chi phí] Staff fixed cash cost 10 tỷ, maintenance 2 tỷ, ngoài training. Không overhead khác.
[Thu tiền] Paid procedures cash collected 28 tỷ; opening AR zero, all earned billed. Grant tiền riêng; cash training/variable/fixed/maintenance all settled.
[Chính sách] Grant release là other operating income; depreciation gross PPE. Charity procedures không tạo consideration nhưng vẫn incur variable expense.
[Báo cáo quản trị] Giám đốc tính 5.000×8 triệu revenue, subtracts grant 80 from PPE rồi vẫn release grant income.

qas.question: Calculate the year-end equipment carrying amount under the gross PPE model.
Find the grant income released during the first six months of use.
Determine closing deferred grant balance.
Find recognized procedure revenue and variable expense; report operating result after all listed charges.
qas.answer: Revenue=32; variable cost=20; result=32+8−20−10−2−3−12=−7 billion VND.

qas.question: Find remaining trade receivable for paid procedures only.
Why would reducing PPE by the grant and releasing deferred grant income under the gross model double-count the subsidy?
qas.answer: The stipulated gross model recognizes PPE 120 and deferred grant 80; it releases income separately. Netting the asset while retaining the same grant release understates depreciation and overstates profit.

qas.question: Can charity procedures be assigned the 8m fee in recognized revenue?
qas.answer: No. They are delivered without customer consideration. Their costs remain included; procedure counts and earned consideration are different.

qas.question: Can the full social return on the donor's investment be estimated?
qas.answer: No. Patient outcomes, alternative treatment cost and social-benefit evidence are missing.

assumptions: Tỷ VND. Công ty hư cấu Cánh Bèo. Toy vehicle head lease ghi liability và ROU. Một phần xe sublease classified operating, retain ROU; không net head lease liability với sublease income. No tax.

evidence.text: [Head lease] Opening ROU carrying 300, lease liability 320. Annual interest 6% opening liability; fixed cash payment 80 cuối năm. No new leases or remeasurement.
[ROU] Remaining life 5 years, straight-line, zero residual. Depreciation on all vehicles regardless of sublease.
[Own operations] Freight revenue 500, cash-type operating expense 400 excludes depreciation/lease interest. All cash received/paid.
[Sublease] 20% fleet subleased full year, rent earned 24, collected 20. Operating sublease classification stipulated, no derecognition. Opening sublease AR zero.
[Cash flow] Interest paid CFO, principal CFF; cash capex unrelated 30; opening unrestricted cash 45. No other financing.
[Policy] Present freight revenue and sublease income gross; ROU depreciation full fleet. No right of offset for sublease AR and head lease liability.
[Deck] Management deducts all 24 sublease income directly from lease principal, calls 80 cash lease payment depreciation.

qas.question: Reconcile head lease interest and principal portions of the annual payment.
Find closing head lease liability after payment.
Find closing ROU carrying amount for the fleet.
Calculate profit before tax including operating sublease, depreciation and interest.
Find closing unrestricted cash using actual sublease collections rather than earned income.
Explain why the 24 sublease income is not a reduction of head lease principal.
qas.answer: It is earned from a separate operating sublease; principal reduction follows the head contract cash and interest allocation, not the sublease revenue.

qas.question: Does subleasing 20% of the fleet mean the same fraction of ROU is automatically derecognized?
qas.answer: No. The case stipulates operating sublease and continuing ROU recognition for the entire fleet.

qas.question: Can future sublease coverage of head-lease payments be guaranteed?
qas.answer: No. The next-year term, collections and subtenant creditworthiness are not supplied.

assumptions: Tỷ VND. Mạng giả lập Hạt Sương. Toy operator A owns 65% physical network asset and bears 65% shared costs, B owns 35%. A acts as payment agent for B's share; no service margin. Reimbursement is receivable recovery, not revenue.

evidence.text: [Hợp đồng sharing] Tổng tower expansion cost 600 tỷ; A pays contractors entire amount, directly owns 65%; B owns 35% and must reimburse A. Assets ready Jan1, life 10 years, no residual.
[Cost sharing] Annual common network operating cost 200; A pays full, B owes 35%. Separate A-only opex 280.
[Collections] B pays 180 toward capital share and 60 toward operating share. All B reimbursements unconditional; opening B AR zero. No other shared balances.
[Service] A's external telecom revenue 700, all collected. No income from B other than cost reimbursement.
[Cash] Opening cash 250, new bank borrowing 300, no debt service; all costs paid cash, no tax.
[Accounting] A capitalizes own asset share, expenses own common operating share, recognizes B's reimbursements as receivables, not gross network sales.
[Deck] CFO books full PPE 600, full common expense 200 and full B billed amounts as revenue to show scale.

qas.question: Find A's qualifying network PPE addition under direct asset ownership.
Find receivable from B for construction costs remaining unpaid.
Find B's unpaid share of annual common operating cost.
Determine A's annual operating profit after its own network costs and depreciation.
Reconcile actual cash closing from construction, common payments, B cash and borrowing.
Why would presenting the 280 billed reimbursements as network revenue misrepresent the business?
qas.answer: A pays on B's behalf, has no margin and directly owns only its share. The 210 capex and 70 opex reimbursements settle claims against B, not customer service consideration.

qas.question: Is B's 35% physical ownership automatically an NCI in A's consolidated equity?
qas.answer: No. It is a direct interest in shared assets, not a stated equity interest in A or its subsidiary.

qas.question: Can coverage expansion per subscriber be assessed from the shared construction cost?
qas.answer: No. Network site count, coverage, subscribers and capacity measures are missing.

assumptions: Triệu USD. Hãng hư cấu Sóng Trắng. Toy engine exchange replaces old component; new engine capitalized at cash + trade-in consideration; old engine derecognized with trade-in credit as proceeds. Separate temporary engine rental expense.

evidence.text: [Engine register] Old engine carrying 18m; exchange supplier grants trade-in credit 12m. New engine agreed price 45m; net cash payable 33m. Exchange on July1, ready for use immediately.

[Accounting] Derecognize old engine for 12m credit, capitalize new 45m; new life 9 years zero residual, depreciate six months. No old engine depreciation current year under toy because prior engine was grounded.
[Rental] Temporary spare leased Jan–Jun at .5m/month, expensed and paid. No lease balance under simplified model.
[Maintenance] Routine inspection cost 2m expensed; qualifying major inspection asset 6m added on Oct1, life 3 years, depreciation 3 months. All paid.
[Operations] Profit before these engine/rental/inspection charges 40m. No tax/interest or other D&A.
[Cash] Opening cash 60m, operating cash surplus before these specific outlays 42m. No other cash flows.
[Deck] CTO reports new engine addition 33m only, leaves old 18m in assets; capitalizes temporary rental and routine inspection.

qas.question: Calculate the loss on derecognition of the old engine.
Find new engine carrying at year-end after six months' depreciation.
Find closing major inspection component carrying.
Calculate operating profit after disposal loss, rental, routine inspection and new depreciation.
Reconcile year-end cash excluding noncash trade-in credit and depreciation.
Why is the new engine cost not simply the 33m cash payment?
qas.answer: The purchase consideration includes the 12m trade-in credit; new cost 45m and old disposal are separate linked entries.

qas.question: Should rental and routine inspection be included in the capitalized replacement asset?
qas.answer: No. The stipulated policy expenses them as current service/maintenance; only new engine and qualifying major inspection are capitalized.

qas.question: Can the remaining aircraft useful life be inferred from the new engine's nine-year life?
qas.answer: No. Component life does not determine the airframe's useful life or regulatory service life.

assumptions: Tỷ VND, nghìn tấn. Nhà máy giả lập Mía Đồi. Toy sugarcane grower contract allocates 55% of net sugar sales proceeds to cane growers as raw material cost, excludes molasses and bagasse revenue; minimum grower payment 300. No tax.

evidence.text: [Production] Process 1.000 nghìn tonnes cane, produce and sell 100 nghìn tonnes sugar at 8 triệu/tấn. Molasses sold 40 nghìn tonnes at 2 triệu/tấn. Bagasse electricity sales 30 tỷ.
[Grower formula] 55% of actual net sugar consideration after sugar-specific selling expense 20 tỷ, subject to annual minimum 300. No share on molasses/electricity. All raw cane consumed.
[Settlement] Advance 350 tỷ paid growers during year, no opening payable; final audited grower amount billed but unpaid portion remains AP.
[Other costs] Conversion cash expense 250 tỷ, central opex 60 tỷ, electricity generation extra cost 10 tỷ. Sugar selling 20 separate; no depreciation beyond amounts.
[Cash] Customer receipts 860, opening AR 40; all external sales billed. All conversion/central/selling/electricity expenses paid. No tax/debt.
[Policy] Grower share is raw material expense, not net revenue reduction; compare actual vs minimum, not additive.
[Deck] Management computes grower share on sugar+molasses+electricity and adds minimum 300 to calculated share.

qas.question: Find total external sugar, molasses and electricity revenue.
Find grower entitlement under the contractual sharing formula.
Find grower payable remaining after the 350 advance.
Calculate mill operating result on the specified gross presentation.
Reconcile closing external trade receivables.
Why not include molasses and electricity proceeds in the grower-sharing denominator?
qas.answer: The signed formula is explicitly limited to net sugar consideration; the byproduct streams are outside the base.

qas.question: Does the minimum payment add 300 to the 429 entitlement?
qas.answer: No. It is a floor, not a separate charge. Entitlement is the greater of the calculated share and minimum.

qas.question: Can profit earned by individual cane growers be established?
qas.answer: No. Individual deliveries, farming costs and allocations are not disclosed.

assumptions: Tỷ VND. Trường giả lập Lam Khê điều phối consortium. Toy pass-through funds held as agent for partner universities; only own qualifying grant expenditure earns grant revenue. Separate coordination fee earned as service.

evidence.text: [Sponsor agreement] Sponsor transfers 150 tỷ: 90 for partner universities, 50 own research eligible spending, 10 fixed coordination fee for annual service. Funds cannot be reallocated without approval.
[Partner settlement] School transfers 70 of the 90 to partners; remaining 20 payable. School does not control partner research and receives no margin.
[Own research] Qualifying expenditure 38 this year (all paid), ineligible expense 4 (paid from own general cash). Remaining 12 own grant refundable if unspent; no extra grant.
[Coordination] Annual service fully delivered, fee 10 earned. Direct coordination cost 6 paid.
[Operations] Other tuition surplus 25 before consortium, cash surplus same. Opening general cash 40, no restricted opening. No tax.
[Policy] Partner transfers settle agency payable; own grant earns on verified eligible cost; ineligible expense not funded from grant. Fee separately earned.
[Deck] Rector treats whole 150 as research revenue, 70 transfers as research expense and unspent 32 as operating surplus.

qas.question: Find own grant revenue earned on approved research expenditure.
Find remaining liability for partner pass-through funding.
Find deferred/refundable own research grant balance.
Find total operating surplus including own research, fee and ineligible cost.
Calculate total ending cash from the disclosed consortium and ordinary activities.
Explain why 32 of remaining restricted/agency cash is not free operating profit.
qas.answer: 20 belongs to partners, 12 is unearned refundable grant funding. Cash is not the same as earned grant or fee income.

qas.question: Should the partner transfers be treated as school research expenses under this toy?
qas.answer: No. The school acts as agent for the 90 partner funds; transfers extinguish the corresponding payable.

qas.question: Can total research outputs per billion of grant be compared across consortium universities?
qas.answer: No. Partner spending and output metrics are not supplied.

assumptions: Triệu USD, thousand tonnes. Công ty hư cấu Đá Ngân. Toy offtake price floor/cap applies only committed contracted tonnes; buyer prepayment allocated equally per tonne delivered, not extra revenue. All output sold.

evidence.text: [Offtake] Buyer agrees purchase 60k tonnes/year at reference price subject to floor $900/t and cap $1,300/t. Opening prepayment liability 30m allocated across 100k cumulative future tonnes at $300/t.
[Current shipment] 60k contracted tonnes delivered when reference $1,500/t, and 40k spot tonnes sold at $1,500/t. No other shipments. All delivery accepted.
[Payment] For contract tonnes, release $300/t prepayment against full agreed sale price; buyer pays remaining invoice in cash this period. Spot buyers pay full.
[Cost] Production cost $700/t on all 100k; royalty 4% of recognized sale consideration; central expense 8m. All expenses paid; no tax.
[Balance] Opening cash 20m; prepayment received prior year, not current cash. No new prepayments, capex or borrowing.
[Policy] Prepayment release forms part of contractual sales consideration, not additional revenue beyond price cap.
[Deck] Trader reports contracted sales at spot $1,500 and adds prepayment release 18m to gross sales.

qas.question: Find current contracted sale consideration under the price cap.
Find release of opening prepayment liability for contracted tonnes delivered.
Find total current cash received from both buyers.
Calculate current royalty expense on recognized consideration.
Find operating profit from current deliveries after all listed costs.
Why does adding the 18m prepayment release to 78m contracted sales double-count consideration?
qas.answer: The 78m contractual price already includes the 18m allocated advance plus 60m new cash. Release is settlement of a liability, not incremental sale price.

qas.question: Can the entire 100k tonnes be priced at the market reference 1500?
qas.answer: No. Only spot 40k earns 1500; contract 60k is capped at 1300.

qas.question: Can future floor/cap economics and total cash collection over the remaining contract be estimated exactly?
qas.answer: No. Future reference prices, timing and volumes beyond the stated commitments are missing.

assumptions: Tỷ VND. Utility giả lập Dòng Xanh. Toy approved regulatory true-up recognized separately from billed revenue when enforceable; later collection of regulatory asset reduces asset, not new revenue. No tax.

evidence.text: [Tariff] 2025 customer billed service 900 tỷ, all earned. Approved allowed revenue requirement 980. Regulator signs binding true-up of 60 from difference, rejects 20. Recovery charged in 2026, no current cash.

[Prior asset] Opening regulatory asset 50 from 2024. Current 2025 bills include separate collection surcharge 30 for opening asset, not included in 900 service revenue. Remaining prior balance recoverable.
[Collections] All 930 invoiced, cash collected 910, opening customer AR 40. No bad debt. Collect surcharge through AR, recognize recovery as reduction of regulatory asset when billed per toy.
[Costs] Opex 650, depreciation 120, interest 40. Cash opex paid 630, interest paid 40; no capex or tax.
[Accounting] Current service revenue 900 plus 60 approved regulatory adjustment as income; 30 collection not revenue. Regulatory asset roll-forward 50+60−30.
[Deck] CFO adds full allowed shortfall 80, surcharge 30 and billed service 900 as current income; calls all regulatory asset cash equivalent.
[Risk] No future tariff collection profile, no impairment assessment or customer credit information.

qas.question: Find enforceable current regulatory adjustment income.
Reconcile closing regulatory asset under the specified billing-release convention.
Find closing customer AR including billed recovery surcharge.
Calculate profit before tax using recognized current income only.
Calculate operating cash generated after interest using actual collections.
Why would including the 30 surcharge again in revenue misstate PBT?
qas.answer: That billing recovers an asset from prior-year recognized income; under the toy it transfers regulatory asset to customer AR rather than earning revenue twice.

qas.question: Can the 80 regulatory asset be used as cash available for immediate debt repayment?
qas.answer: No. It is a future collection right; current liquidity requires actual cash and collection timing.

qas.question: Can the 20 rejected amount be recognized later if the regulator reverses its decision?
qas.answer: Only conditionally with new enforceable approval. No such approval exists at reporting date; future outcome cannot be determined.
